logs	quick	sudo docker compose -p mailcowdockerized logs --tail 500 --timestamps
backup	long	sudo /opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh

internalTLSSetupSteps:
log "Mailcow: installing into /opt/mailcow-dockerized"
if [ ! -d "/opt/mailcow-dockerized/.git" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "/opt/mailcow-dockerized" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  # Kept data, no repository: bring the repository in beside it.
  rm -rf "/opt/mailcow-dockerized.clone"
  git clone --no-checkout https://github.com/mailcow/mailcow-dockerized "/opt/mailcow-dockerized.clone"
  mv "/opt/mailcow-dockerized.clone/.git" "/opt/mailcow-dockerized/.git"
  rm -rf "/opt/mailcow-dockerized.clone"
  git -C "/opt/mailcow-dockerized" checkout HEAD -- .
elif [ ! -d "/opt/mailcow-dockerized/.git" ]; then
  git clone https://github.com/mailcow/mailcow-dockerized /opt/mailcow-dockerized
fi
cd /opt/mailcow-dockerized
if [ ! -f mailcow.conf ]; then
  # Non-interactive config: hostname/timezone/branch via env. The env
  # vars do NOT cover everything: on low-memory hosts (≤ 2.5 GiB) the
  # script still prompts "disable ClamAV? [Y/n]" (and similar) from
  # stdin, hanging a headless run. Feed a bounded set of yes-answers:
  # unexpected prompts read them (or hit EOF → their default), and a
  # bounded printf can't die of SIGPIPE under pipefail.
  # COMPOSE_VERSION: generate_config.sh does not detect the compose
  # flavour, it only substitutes this variable into mailcow.conf. We
  # install the compose plugin, so it is always "native".
  printf 'y\ny\ny\n' | COMPOSE_VERSION=native MAILCOW_HOSTNAME=mail.example.com MAILCOW_TZ=UTC MAILCOW_BRANCH=master ./generate_config.sh
  # Behind the shared Caddy ingress: web UI on loopback only.
  sed -i 's/^HTTP_BIND=.*/HTTP_BIND=127.0.0.1/' mailcow.conf
  sed -i 's/^HTTP_PORT=.*/HTTP_PORT=8080/' mailcow.conf
  sed -i 's/^HTTPS_BIND=.*/HTTPS_BIND=127.0.0.1/' mailcow.conf
  sed -i 's/^HTTPS_PORT=.*/HTTPS_PORT=18443/' mailcow.conf
  # TLS terminates at Caddy; mailcow must not fight for ACME.
  sed -i 's/^SKIP_LETS_ENCRYPT=.*/SKIP_LETS_ENCRYPT=y/' mailcow.conf
fi
# Left empty, DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION takes every mailcow helper that
# reads it down with it: `backup_and_restore.sh restore` aborts with
# "Can not read DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION variable from mailcow.conf"
# BEFORE unpacking anything, so the restore wrapper reports failure
# having restored nothing (update.sh is safe — it unsets and re-detects
# the value itself). Repaired here, outside the `if` above, because the
# conf is generated exactly once: servers installed before this fix are
# only reachable through a setup re-run, which is how sudoers and
# wrapper changes already reach them.
if grep -q '^DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=' mailcow.conf; then
  sed -i 's/^DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=.*/DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=native/' mailcow.conf
else
  echo 'DOCKER_COMPOSE_VERSION=native' >> mailcow.conf
fi
# A clone made under a tight umask stays broken forever without this:
# git has no mode flag, and a re-run skips the clone (.git is already
# there). mailcow's containers drop to their own users — nginx's config
# says `user nginx` — and mount this tree, so root-only modes make the
# worker fail to even traverse /web and every PHP path answers a bare
# nginx 404, the whole API included. mailcow.conf keeps 600: it holds
# the database passwords.
chmod -R a+rX .
chmod 600 mailcow.conf
# Pull/up wrapped in retry: on a fresh public server the first pull of
# mailcow's ~15 images often trips a transient registry timeout, which
# under `set -e` aborted the install and forced a manual Retry.
retry 4 docker compose pull -q
retry 2 docker compose up -d

cd /opt/mailcow-dockerized
# Enable the REST API once (key generated on this server, kept by
# re-runs). docker-compose passes API_KEY/API_ALLOW_FROM into the php
# container; the last assignment in the .env-style file wins, so
# appending works even next to the commented template lines.
if ! grep -q '^API_KEY=' mailcow.conf; then
  # The caller is the host reaching the published port, so mailcow's
  # nginx sees the connection arrive from its own bridge gateway — .1
  # of whatever IPV4_NETWORK generate_config.sh settled on. That is
  # 172.22.1 by default but NOT always: the generator moves the subnet
  # when it collides with a docker network that already exists, and a
  # hardcoded gateway then fails the API's IP ACL with an "api access
  # denied for ip" that reads exactly like a wrong key.
  MC_NET="$(grep '^IPV4_NETWORK=' mailcow.conf | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  printf 'API_KEY=%s\nAPI_ALLOW_FROM=%s.1,127.0.0.1\n' \
    "$(openssl rand -hex 20)" "${MC_NET:-172.22.1}" >> mailcow.conf
  docker compose up -d
fi
MC_API_KEY="$(grep '^API_KEY=' mailcow.conf | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
MC_API="https://127.0.0.1:18443/api/v1"
MC_BODY="$(mktemp)"
MC_CODE=000
# The API lives on the HTTPS vhost. mailcow's HTTP port 301-redirects
# to it unconditionally, and curl without -L returns the redirect's
# HTML body instead of JSON — so every call over HTTP silently failed
# (jq found no fields), add/domain and add/dkim never ran, and DKIM was
# reported "not ready" forever. Hit HTTPS directly, -k for self-signed.
#
# Status into a variable, body into a file, and never a non-zero exit.
# With `curl -f` the only thing that reached the install log was
# "curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404": the body — which
# is mailcow's own reason for refusing ("route not found",
# "authentication failed", "Cannot find attributes in post data") — was
# discarded, so the failure was undiagnosable, and the bare exit status
# killed the entire 22-step install under `set -e` at step 7, before
# the other services and before the install key was revoked.
mc_api() {
  MC_CODE="$(curl -sSk --max-time 20 -o "$MC_BODY" -w '%{http_code}' -K - \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" "$@" <<< "header = \"X-API-Key: $MC_API_KEY\"")" || :
  case "$MC_CODE" in ''|*[!0-9]*) MC_CODE=000 ;; esac
  [ "$MC_CODE" -ge 200 ] && [ "$MC_CODE" -lt 300 ]
}
# Why the last call failed, in one bounded line: an HTML error page
# instead of JSON must not flood the log the app streams.
mc_why() { printf 'HTTP %s %s' "$MC_CODE" "$(tr -d '\r\n' < "$MC_BODY" | cut -c1-300)"; }
log "Mailcow: adding domain example.com and its DKIM key over the API"
# A deadline rather than a fixed number of tries: each attempt can
# itself burn the 20 s curl timeout, so counting attempts bounded this
# wait at 25 minutes of total silence, not the 5 it was meant to be.
MC_READY=0
MC_TRY=0
MC_DEADLINE=$(($(date +%s) + 300))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$MC_DEADLINE" ]; do
  if mc_api "$MC_API/get/domain/all"; then MC_READY=1; break; fi
  # Heartbeat every ~30 s. The API needs a while after the containers
  # report healthy, and a wait that prints nothing at all is
  # indistinguishable from a hung install in the app's progress view.
  MC_TRY=$((MC_TRY + 1))
  if [ "$((MC_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Mailcow: waiting for the API to come up ($(mc_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$MC_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  # Every mail domain (the primary one plus any additional
  # domains) with its own DKIM key. Both steps are idempotent — created
  # only when missing, so re-runs never touch an existing configuration,
  # and a domain removed from the app is left alone on the server rather
  # than deleted with its mailboxes.
  # The list is fed through a here-document rather than a quoted word
  # list: it reads the names literally, so no shell quoting question
  # arises at all, and it stays the same shape for one domain or ten.
  while IFS= read -r MC_DOMAIN; do
    [ -n "$MC_DOMAIN" ] || continue
    if ! mc_api "$MC_API/get/domain/$MC_DOMAIN" || ! jq -e '.domain_name' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mc_api -X POST -d "{\"domain\":\"$MC_DOMAIN\",\"description\":\"Managed by gryonixNexus\",\"aliases\":\"400\",\"defquota\":\"3072\",\"maxquota\":\"10240\",\"quota\":\"10240\",\"mailboxes\":\"50\",\"active\":\"1\",\"restart_sogo\":\"10\"}" \
        "$MC_API/add/domain" \
        || log "Mailcow: could not add domain $MC_DOMAIN over the API — add it under Configuration → Domains in the admin UI. ($(mc_why))"
    fi
    if ! mc_api "$MC_API/get/dkim/$MC_DOMAIN" || ! jq -e '.pubkey' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mc_api -X POST -d "{\"domains\":\"$MC_DOMAIN\",\"dkim_selector\":\"dkim\",\"key_size\":2048}" \
        "$MC_API/add/dkim" \
        || log "Mailcow: could not create the DKIM key for $MC_DOMAIN over the API — create it under Configuration → ARC/DKIM keys in the admin UI. ($(mc_why))"
    fi
  done <<'EOF_MC_DOMAINS'
example.com
example.org
EOF_MC_DOMAINS
  # The panel's `admin` ships with a published password. Replace it once
  # the API answers (the admin row exists by then) and keep the new one
  # in a root-only file the report reads; a failed call keeps the default
  # and the report says so. Re-runs reuse the stored password.
  MC_ADMIN_FILE="/opt/mailcow-dockerized/.gryonixnexus-admin-password"
  MC_ADMIN_PASS="$(cat "$MC_ADMIN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [ -n "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" ] || MC_ADMIN_PASS="$(openssl rand -hex 12)"
  MC_REQ="$(mktemp)"
  printf '{"items":["admin"],"attr":{"password":"%s","password2":"%s"}}' "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" > "$MC_REQ"
  if mc_api -X POST -d @"$MC_REQ" \
       "$MC_API/edit/admin" \
     && jq -e 'if type == "array" then all(.[]; .type == "success") else .type == "success" end' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    (umask 077; printf '%s\n' "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" > "$MC_ADMIN_FILE")
  else
    log "Mailcow admin password: the default one stays ($(mc_why))"
  fi
  rm -f "$MC_REQ"
else
  log "Mailcow: the API did not answer — the domain and DKIM key were NOT created. Mailcow itself is running: add the domain under Configuration → Domains in its admin UI, or re-run the setup. ($(mc_why))"
fi
rm -f "$MC_BODY"

# Automatic trusted TLS for SMTP/IMAPS. Caddy fronts only the web UI;
# mailcow's mail daemons (Postfix/Dovecot) serve their OWN certificate,
# so without this they present a self-signed one and mail clients warn.
# Sync Caddy's issued certificate for mail.example.com into mailcow's ssl
# assets and reload the mail daemons — once now (a no-op until Caddy has
# issued it) and then on a timer so renewals are picked up automatically.
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh <<'EOF_MC_CERTSYNC'
#!/bin/bash
set -eu
DOMAIN="mail.example.com"
MAILCOW="/opt/mailcow-dockerized"
DEST="$MAILCOW/data/assets/ssl"
CADDY_DATA="/var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates"
SRC_CRT="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.crt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
SRC_KEY="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.key" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
if [ -z "$SRC_CRT" ] || [ -z "$SRC_KEY" ]; then exit 0; fi
if cmp -s "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem" && cmp -s "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"; then exit 0; fi
cp "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem"
cp "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"
cd "$MAILCOW"
docker compose restart postfix-mailcow dovecot-mailcow nginx-mailcow >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
EOF_MC_CERTSYNC
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.service <<'EOF_MC_CERTSVC'
[Unit]
Description=Sync Caddy TLS certificate into Mailcow (SMTP/IMAPS)
After=docker.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh
EOF_MC_CERTSVC
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer <<'EOF_MC_CERTTIMER'
[Unit]
Description=Periodic Caddy to Mailcow TLS certificate sync
[Timer]
OnActiveSec=5min
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
Persistent=true
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF_MC_CERTTIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh || true

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
CONF="/opt/mailcow-dockerized/mailcow.conf"
[ -r "$CONF" ] || { echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"; exit 0; }
MC_KEY="$(grep '^API_KEY=' "$CONF" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
API="https://127.0.0.1:18443/api/v1"
mc() { curl -fsSk --max-time 20 -K - "$@" <<< "header = \"X-API-Key: $MC_KEY\""; }
DOMAINS="$({ mc "$API/get/domain/all" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].domain_name // empty' 2>/dev/null || true; mc "$API/get/alias-domain/all" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].alias_domain // empty' 2>/dev/null || true; } | sort -u)"
dkim_of() { mc "$API/get/dkim/$1" 2>/dev/null | jq -r "select(type == \"object\") | .$2 // empty" 2>/dev/null || true; }
for D in $DOMAINS; do
  if [ -z "$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_txt)" ]; then
    mc -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"domains\":\"$D\",\"dkim_selector\":\"dkim\",\"key_size\":2048}" "$API/add/dkim" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  TXT="$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_txt)"
  SEL="$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_selector)"
  if [ -n "$TXT" ]; then echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM ${SEL:-dkim}._domainkey.$D $TXT"; fi
done
echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"
EOF_GD_DKIM
chmod 750 /opt/gryonixnexus-dkim.sh

  # Heartbeat every ~30 s. The API needs a while after the containers
  # report healthy, and a wait that prints nothing at all is
  # indistinguishable from a hung install in the app's progress view.
  MC_TRY=$((MC_TRY + 1))
  if [ "$((MC_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Mailcow: waiting for the API to come up ($(mc_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$MC_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  # Every mail domain (the primary one plus any additional
  # domains) with its own DKIM key. Both steps are idempotent — created
  # only when missing, so re-runs never touch an existing configuration,
  # and a domain removed from the app is left alone on the server rather
  # than deleted with its mailboxes.
  # The list is fed through a here-document rather than a quoted word
  # list: it reads the names literally, so no shell quoting question
  # arises at all, and it stays the same shape for one domain or ten.
  while IFS= read -r MC_DOMAIN; do
    [ -n "$MC_DOMAIN" ] || continue
    if ! mc_api "$MC_API/get/domain/$MC_DOMAIN" || ! jq -e '.domain_name' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mc_api -X POST -d "{\"domain\":\"$MC_DOMAIN\",\"description\":\"Managed by gryonixNexus\",\"aliases\":\"400\",\"defquota\":\"3072\",\"maxquota\":\"10240\",\"quota\":\"10240\",\"mailboxes\":\"50\",\"active\":\"1\",\"restart_sogo\":\"10\"}" \
        "$MC_API/add/domain" \
        || log "Mailcow: could not add domain $MC_DOMAIN over the API — add it under Configuration → Domains in the admin UI. ($(mc_why))"
    fi
    if ! mc_api "$MC_API/get/dkim/$MC_DOMAIN" || ! jq -e '.pubkey' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      mc_api -X POST -d "{\"domains\":\"$MC_DOMAIN\",\"dkim_selector\":\"dkim\",\"key_size\":2048}" \
        "$MC_API/add/dkim" \
        || log "Mailcow: could not create the DKIM key for $MC_DOMAIN over the API — create it under Configuration → ARC/DKIM keys in the admin UI. ($(mc_why))"
    fi
  done <<'EOF_MC_DOMAINS'
example.com
example.org
EOF_MC_DOMAINS
  # The panel's `admin` ships with a published password. Replace it once
  # the API answers (the admin row exists by then) and keep the new one
  # in a root-only file the report reads; a failed call keeps the default
  # and the report says so. Re-runs reuse the stored password.
  MC_ADMIN_FILE="/opt/mailcow-dockerized/.gryonixnexus-admin-password"
  MC_ADMIN_PASS="$(cat "$MC_ADMIN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [ -n "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" ] || MC_ADMIN_PASS="$(openssl rand -hex 12)"
  MC_REQ="$(mktemp)"
  printf '{"items":["admin"],"attr":{"password":"%s","password2":"%s"}}' "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" > "$MC_REQ"
  if mc_api -X POST -d @"$MC_REQ" \
       "$MC_API/edit/admin" \
     && jq -e 'if type == "array" then all(.[]; .type == "success") else .type == "success" end' < "$MC_BODY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    (umask 077; printf '%s\n' "$MC_ADMIN_PASS" > "$MC_ADMIN_FILE")
  else
    log "Mailcow admin password: the default one stays ($(mc_why))"
  fi
  rm -f "$MC_REQ"
else
  log "Mailcow: the API did not answer — the domain and DKIM key were NOT created. Mailcow itself is running: add the domain under Configuration → Domains in its admin UI, or re-run the setup. ($(mc_why))"
fi
rm -f "$MC_BODY"

# Automatic trusted TLS for SMTP/IMAPS. Caddy fronts only the web UI;
# mailcow's mail daemons (Postfix/Dovecot) serve their OWN certificate,
# so without this they present a self-signed one and mail clients warn.
# Sync Caddy's issued certificate for mail.example.com into mailcow's ssl
# assets and reload the mail daemons — once now (a no-op until Caddy has
# issued it) and then on a timer so renewals are picked up automatically.
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh <<'EOF_MC_CERTSYNC'
#!/bin/bash
set -eu
DOMAIN="mail.example.com"
MAILCOW="/opt/mailcow-dockerized"
DEST="$MAILCOW/data/assets/ssl"
CADDY_DATA="/var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates"
SRC_CRT="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.crt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
SRC_KEY="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.key" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
if [ -z "$SRC_CRT" ] || [ -z "$SRC_KEY" ]; then exit 0; fi
if cmp -s "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem" && cmp -s "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"; then exit 0; fi
cp "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem"
cp "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"
cd "$MAILCOW"
docker compose restart postfix-mailcow dovecot-mailcow nginx-mailcow >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
EOF_MC_CERTSYNC
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.service <<'EOF_MC_CERTSVC'
[Unit]
Description=Sync Caddy TLS certificate into Mailcow (SMTP/IMAPS)
After=docker.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh
EOF_MC_CERTSVC
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer <<'EOF_MC_CERTTIMER'
[Unit]
Description=Periodic Caddy to Mailcow TLS certificate sync
[Timer]
OnActiveSec=5min
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
Persistent=true
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF_MC_CERTTIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/opt/gryonixnexus-mailcow-cert-sync.sh || true

# Root-owned DKIM dump: every domain and alias domain, missing keys created.
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-dkim.sh <<'EOF_GD_DKIM'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
CONF="/opt/mailcow-dockerized/mailcow.conf"
[ -r "$CONF" ] || { echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"; exit 0; }
MC_KEY="$(grep '^API_KEY=' "$CONF" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)"
API="https://127.0.0.1:18443/api/v1"
mc() { curl -fsSk --max-time 20 -K - "$@" <<< "header = \"X-API-Key: $MC_KEY\""; }
DOMAINS="$({ mc "$API/get/domain/all" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].domain_name // empty' 2>/dev/null || true; mc "$API/get/alias-domain/all" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[].alias_domain // empty' 2>/dev/null || true; } | sort -u)"
dkim_of() { mc "$API/get/dkim/$1" 2>/dev/null | jq -r "select(type == \"object\") | .$2 // empty" 2>/dev/null || true; }
for D in $DOMAINS; do
  if [ -z "$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_txt)" ]; then
    mc -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"domains\":\"$D\",\"dkim_selector\":\"dkim\",\"key_size\":2048}" "$API/add/dkim" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  TXT="$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_txt)"
  SEL="$(dkim_of "$D" dkim_selector)"
  if [ -n "$TXT" ]; then echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM ${SEL:-dkim}._domainkey.$D $TXT"; fi
done
echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"
EOF_GD_DKIM
chmod 750 /opt/gryonixnexus-dkim.sh

    image: redis:8-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:

  front:
    image: ghcr.io/mailu/nginx:2024.06
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env
    logging:
      driver: json-file
    ports:
      # The web UI stays on loopback behind Caddy; the mail ports
      # are the only public binds, and they are not proxyable —

      # PORT_143/PORT_587 and binds them to port 0 when unset,

      # the public interface, because docker publishes through
      # its own DNAT, past the firewall.

      - "465:465"

    image: ghcr.io/mailu/unbound:2024.06

envTemplate:
# Managed by gryonixNexus. Generated on the server; secrets are the
# __RANDOM__ markers, replaced once and then left alone on re-runs.
SECRET_KEY=__RANDOM__
DOMAIN=example.com
HOSTNAMES=mail.example.com,mail.example.org
POSTMASTER=postmaster
# See the type comment: Caddy owns 80/443 and the ACME account, so Mailu
# serves plain HTTP for the proxy and uses the synced certificate for
# SMTP/IMAP only.
TLS_FLAVOR=mail
SUBNET=10.254.29.0/24
# The first administrator is created by the stack itself. `ifmissing`
# rather than `update`: a re-run of setup must not reset a password the
# owner has since changed.
INITIAL_ADMIN_ACCOUNT=admin
INITIAL_ADMIN_DOMAIN=example.com
INITIAL_ADMIN_PW=__RANDOM__
INITIAL_ADMIN_MODE=ifmissing
# Behind a proxy Mailu would otherwise log and rate-limit Caddy's
# address instead of the client's.
#
# The trusted address is the BRIDGE GATEWAY, not 127.0.0.1: Caddy
# connects to a published port on the host, and the container sees that
# connection arriving from the docker network's gateway. This is the
# same trap as mailcow's API_ALLOW_FROM — a loopback
# value here does not fail loudly, it silently makes every client look
# like the proxy, which means the per-IP rate limit bans everyone at
# once the first time one client gets a password wrong.
REAL_IP_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For
REAL_IP_FROM=10.254.29.1
WEBROOT_REDIRECT=/webmail
# ADMIN gates the admin interface ITSELF, WEB_ADMIN only says where it
# would live. Without this the nginx template renders no location for
# it at all: /admin falls through to WEBROOT_REDIRECT and lands on the
# webmail, which reads as "the admin UI is broken". The setup report points at /admin.
ADMIN=true
WEB_ADMIN=/admin
WEB_WEBMAIL=/webmail
WEBMAIL=roundcube
WEBDAV=none
# Off deliberately: ClamAV alone wants about a gigabyte of RAM, which is
# most of a small server's headroom. Rspamd still filters spam.
ANTIVIRUS=none
MESSAGE_SIZE_LIMIT=50000000
RECIPIENT_DELIMITER=+
DMARC_RUA=postmaster
DMARC_RUF=postmaster
COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=mailu
MAILU_HOSTNAME=mail.example.com

# their own uids and do not need host accounts reading them.

# chowns its own mounts before dropping privileges (`admin` runs

#!/bin/bash
set -eu
DOMAIN="mail.example.com"
MAILU="/opt/mailu"
DEST="$MAILU/certs"
CADDY_DATA="/var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates"
SRC_CRT="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.crt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
SRC_KEY="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.key" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"

# comes back every hour and the mail ports keep serving the old one.

if cmp -s "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem" && cmp -s "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"; then exit 0; fi

cp "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"
chmod 600 "$DEST/cert.pem" "$DEST/key.pem"
cd "$MAILU"
# Only the services that terminate TLS themselves; restarting the whole
# project would drop deliveries in flight for nothing.
docker compose -p mailu restart front >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
EOF_MU_CERTSYNC

# Domains and DKIM keys. Nothing here is fatal and no output is
# discarded — the same rule the mailcow API and Nextcloud occ
# blocks follow: errexit in the middle of this step would take the
# remaining services and the revocation of the install key with it,
# and a mail domain is fixable from the admin UI afterwards.
# Its own cd: sections share one shell and the working directory
# persists across them, so relying on an earlier step's cd is a
# dependency nobody can see when the steps are reordered.
cd /opt/mailu
MU_OUT=""
# `-u`: never as root — see `adminRunAsUser`. A root exec here
# creates /data/main.db before the engine does, and the engine
# then cannot write its own schema into it.
mu_exec() { MU_OUT="$(timeout 120 docker compose -p mailu exec -T -u mailu admin "$@" 2>&1)"; }
mu_why() { printf '%s' "$MU_OUT" | tr -d '\r\n' | cut -c1-300; }
# A deadline, not a number of attempts: each attempt can burn its
# own timeout, so counting attempts leaves the real wait unbounded.
# `flask mailu config-export` has to reach the database, which is
# what is actually not ready yet while the containers report up.
MU_READY=0
MU_TRY=0
MU_DEADLINE=$(($(date +%s) + 300))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$MU_DEADLINE" ]; do
  if mu_exec flask mailu config-export -j; then MU_READY=1; break; fi
  MU_TRY=$((MU_TRY + 1))
  # Heartbeat every ~30 s: silence here is indistinguishable from a
  # hung install in the app's progress view.
  if [ "$((MU_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Mailu: waiting for the admin service to answer ($(mu_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$MU_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  # `-u` is merge mode, and it is not optional: without it the
  # input is treated as the configuration rather than an addition
  # to it. `-q` because the app streams this log.
  #
  # The key is `domain`, singular — the same name the export uses.
  # A plural one is not an error the tool reports, it is simply a
  # section nothing reads, so the keys would never be minted.
  #
  # Idempotent for this shape: `-generate-` mints a key only where
  # there is none, so a re-run leaves existing keys alone.
  if ! printf '%s\n' 'domain:' '  - name: example.com
    dkim_key: -generate-
  - name: example.org
    dkim_key: -generate-' \
       | timeout 120 docker compose -p mailu exec -T -u mailu admin \
         flask mailu config-import -q -u >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "Mailu: the mail domains were NOT created. Mailu itself is running: add them under Domains in its admin UI, or re-run the setup."
  fi
else
  log "Mailu did not answer in time — the mail domains and DKIM keys were not created; check the container logs ($(mu_why))"
fi

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-mailu-dkim.sh <<'EOF_GD_MU_DKIM'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
cd /opt/mailu 2>/dev/null || { echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"; exit 0; }
# --dns asks Mailu for the records it would publish; the private key is
# NOT in that projection, which is why this dump can be whitelisted.
OUT="$(timeout 60 docker compose -p mailu exec -T -u mailu admin \
       flask mailu config-export -d -j domain 2>/dev/null || true)"
printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    data = json.load(sys.stdin)
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit(0)
for domain in data.get("domain", []):
    record = domain.get("dns_dkim")
    if not record:
        continue
    # dns_dkim is a full zone line: "<name> 600 IN TXT \"v=DKIM1…\"".
    # The app wants the name and the value, so keep those two.
    name, _, rest = record.partition(" ")
    value = rest[rest.find("\"") :].strip() if "\"" in rest else rest.strip()
    print("GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM " + name.rstrip(".") + " " + value)

#!/bin/bash
set -eu
DOMAIN="mail.example.com"
MAILU="/opt/mailu"
DEST="$MAILU/certs"
CADDY_DATA="/var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates"
SRC_CRT="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.crt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
SRC_KEY="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.key" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
# No certificate yet (ACME still pending) is not an error: the timer
# comes back every hour and the mail ports keep serving the old one.
if [ -z "$SRC_CRT" ] || [ -z "$SRC_KEY" ]; then exit 0; fi
if cmp -s "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem" && cmp -s "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"; then exit 0; fi
cp "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem"
cp "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"
chmod 600 "$DEST/cert.pem" "$DEST/key.pem"
cd "$MAILU"
# Only the services that terminate TLS themselves; restarting the whole
# project would drop deliveries in flight for nothing.
docker compose -p mailu restart front >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-mailu-cert-sync.timer <<'EOF_MU_CERTTIMER'

Description=Periodic Caddy to Mailu TLS certificate sync
[Timer]
OnActiveSec=5min
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
Persistent=true
[Install]

EOF_MU_CERTTIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now gryonixnexus-mailu-cert-sync.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/opt/gryonixnexus-mailu-cert-sync.sh || true

# Domains and DKIM keys. Nothing here is fatal and no output is
# discarded — the same rule the mailcow API and Nextcloud occ
# blocks follow: errexit in the middle of this step would take the
# remaining services and the revocation of the install key with it,
# and a mail domain is fixable from the admin UI afterwards.
# Its own cd: sections share one shell and the working directory
# persists across them, so relying on an earlier step's cd is a
# dependency nobody can see when the steps are reordered.
cd /opt/mailu
MU_OUT=""
# `-u`: never as root — see `adminRunAsUser`. A root exec here
# creates /data/main.db before the engine does, and the engine
# then cannot write its own schema into it.
mu_exec() { MU_OUT="$(timeout 120 docker compose -p mailu exec -T -u mailu admin "$@" 2>&1)"; }
mu_why() { printf '%s' "$MU_OUT" | tr -d '\r\n' | cut -c1-300; }
# A deadline, not a number of attempts: each attempt can burn its
# own timeout, so counting attempts leaves the real wait unbounded.
# `flask mailu config-export` has to reach the database, which is
# what is actually not ready yet while the containers report up.
MU_READY=0
MU_TRY=0
MU_DEADLINE=$(($(date +%s) + 300))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$MU_DEADLINE" ]; do
  if mu_exec flask mailu config-export -j; then MU_READY=1; break; fi
  MU_TRY=$((MU_TRY + 1))
  # Heartbeat every ~30 s: silence here is indistinguishable from a
  # hung install in the app's progress view.
  if [ "$((MU_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Mailu: waiting for the admin service to answer ($(mu_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$MU_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  # `-u` is merge mode, and it is not optional: without it the
  # input is treated as the configuration rather than an addition
  # to it. `-q` because the app streams this log.
  #
  # The key is `domain`, singular — the same name the export uses.
  # A plural one is not an error the tool reports, it is simply a
  # section nothing reads, so the keys would never be minted.
  #
  # Idempotent for this shape: `-generate-` mints a key only where
  # there is none, so a re-run leaves existing keys alone.
  if ! printf '%s\n' 'domain:' '  - name: example.com
    dkim_key: -generate-
  - name: example.org
    dkim_key: -generate-' \
       | timeout 120 docker compose -p mailu exec -T -u mailu admin \
         flask mailu config-import -q -u >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "Mailu: the mail domains were NOT created. Mailu itself is running: add them under Domains in its admin UI, or re-run the setup."
  fi
else
  log "Mailu did not answer in time — the mail domains and DKIM keys were not created; check the container logs ($(mu_why))"
fi

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-mailu-dkim.sh <<'EOF_GD_MU_DKIM'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
cd /opt/mailu 2>/dev/null || { echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"; exit 0; }
# --dns asks Mailu for the records it would publish; the private key is
# NOT in that projection, which is why this dump can be whitelisted.
OUT="$(timeout 60 docker compose -p mailu exec -T -u mailu admin \
       flask mailu config-export -d -j domain 2>/dev/null || true)"
printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    data = json.load(sys.stdin)
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit(0)
for domain in data.get("domain", []):
    record = domain.get("dns_dkim")
    if not record:
        continue
    # dns_dkim is a full zone line: "<name> 600 IN TXT \"v=DKIM1…\"".
    # The app wants the name and the value, so keep those two.
    name, _, rest = record.partition(" ")
    value = rest[rest.find("\"") :].strip() if "\"" in rest else rest.strip()
    print("GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM " + name.rstrip(".") + " " + value)
' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"
EOF_GD_MU_DKIM
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-mailu-dkim.sh

composeContents:
services:
  mailserver:
    image: ghcr.io/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver:15.1.0
    container_name: mailserver
    hostname: mail.example.com
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env
    # Every client port, including the STARTTLS pair. This engine
    # serves them all, so opening them is honest here.
    ports:
      - "25:25"
      - "143:143"
      - "465:465"
      - "587:587"
      - "993:993"
      - "4190:4190"
    volumes:
      - /opt/docker-mailserver/mail-data:/var/mail
      - /opt/docker-mailserver/mail-state:/var/mail-state
      - /opt/docker-mailserver/mail-logs:/var/log/mail
      - /opt/docker-mailserver/config:/tmp/docker-mailserver
      - /opt/docker-mailserver/certs:/etc/gryonixnexus-certs:ro
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
    # The container answers to its own certificate name INSIDE the
    # compose network. Roundcube verifies the peer name (PHP does
    # by default and Roundcube leaves imap_conn_options unset), so
    # connecting to `mailserver` failed against a certificate
    # issued for mail.example.com. Aliasing here fixes
    # the name instead of switching verification off.
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - mail.example.com
    # Postfix and Dovecot change kernel-visible limits and need to
    # drop privileges themselves; this is the capability set
    # upstream documents for a non-privileged run.
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    stop_grace_period: 1m
  webmail:
    image: roundcube/roundcubemail:1.6.17-apache
    container_name: mailserver-webmail
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - mailserver
    environment:
      # The mail container's alias, not its service name: this
      # name is what the certificate is issued for, and the
      # connection is verified. It still resolves inside the
      # compose network, so the traffic never leaves the host and
      # never touches the published ports.
      ROUNDCUBEMAIL_DEFAULT_HOST: ssl://mail.example.com
      ROUNDCUBEMAIL_DEFAULT_PORT: "993"
      ROUNDCUBEMAIL_SMTP_SERVER: tls://mail.example.com
      ROUNDCUBEMAIL_SMTP_PORT: "587"
      ROUNDCUBEMAIL_PLUGINS: archive,zipdownload,managesieve
      ROUNDCUBEMAIL_UPLOAD_MAX_FILESIZE: 25M
    volumes:
      - /opt/docker-mailserver/webmail:/var/roundcube/config
      # /var/roundcube/db is where the image puts its sqlite file
      # (ROUNDCUBEMAIL_DB_DIR); mounted anywhere else the database
      # stays in the container layer and every recreate throws
      # away the users' settings, contacts and address book.
      - /opt/docker-mailserver/webmail-db:/var/roundcube/db
    ports:
      # Loopback only: Caddy terminates TLS in front of it, which
      # also puts it under the lockdown guard like every other UI.
      - "127.0.0.1:8086:80"
envTemplate:
# Managed by gryonixNexus. Generated on the server; the __RANDOM__ marker
# is replaced once and then left alone on re-runs.
OVERRIDE_HOSTNAME=mail.example.com
POSTMASTER_ADDRESS=postmaster@example.com
# The certificate is handed in by the sync timer below — Caddy owns the
# ACME account on this host, and only one process can.
SSL_TYPE=manual
SSL_CERT_PATH=/etc/gryonixnexus-certs/cert.pem
SSL_KEY_PATH=/etc/gryonixnexus-certs/key.pem
# Rspamd is the modern filter and it also signs DKIM; Amavis, ClamAV and
# SpamAssassin are the legacy chain and together they are most of the
# memory this engine was chosen to avoid. ClamAV alone wants about a
# gigabyte, which is most of a small server's headroom.
ENABLE_RSPAMD=1
ENABLE_OPENDKIM=0
ENABLE_AMAVIS=0
ENABLE_CLAMAV=0
ENABLE_SPAMASSASSIN=0
# Sieve on 4190, the same port the other engines publish.
ENABLE_MANAGESIEVE=1
# No fail2ban: it needs NET_ADMIN plus host firewall access, and the
# deployment already has nftables in front of this container.
ENABLE_FAIL2BAN=0
# Mailboxes live in a file the wrapper edits — no LDAP, no OIDC.
ACCOUNT_PROVISIONER=FILE
# Only the webmail container may relay without authenticating, and it
# reaches Postfix over the compose network.
PERMIT_DOCKER=connected-networks
POSTFIX_MESSAGE_SIZE_LIMIT=50000000
FIRST_MAILBOX_PASSWORD=__RANDOM__

# engine prints "File … does not exist!", shuts down, and

# so on a fresh install there is nothing to point at yet — and a
# container stuck in that loop never gets its first mailbox or its
# DKIM keys either. A self-signed placeholder lets the engine boot;
# the sync below replaces it the moment Caddy has the real one.
# Live-found: without this the whole engine never starts.

       -subj "/CN=mail.example.com" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:mail.example.com" \
       -keyout /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/key.pem -out /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/cert.pem >/dev/null 2>&1; then

  fi

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh <<'EOF_DMS_CERTSYNC'
#!/bin/bash
set -eu
DOMAIN="mail.example.com"
DMS="/opt/docker-mailserver"
DEST="$DMS/certs"
CADDY_DATA="/var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates"
SRC_CRT="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.crt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
SRC_KEY="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.key" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
# No certificate yet (ACME still pending) is not an error: the timer
# comes back every hour and the mail ports keep serving what they have.
if [ -z "$SRC_CRT" ] || [ -z "$SRC_KEY" ]; then exit 0; fi
if cmp -s "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem" && cmp -s "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"; then exit 0; fi
cp "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem"
cp "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"
chmod 644 "$DEST/cert.pem"
chmod 600 "$DEST/key.pem"
cd "$DMS"
# Postfix and Dovecot read the certificate at start; the container has
# no reload hook for a file that changed under it.
docker compose -p dockermailserver restart mailserver >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
EOF_DMS_CERTSYNC
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.service <<'EOF_DMS_CERTSVC'
[Unit]
Description=Sync Caddy TLS certificate into Docker Mailserver (SMTP/IMAPS)
After=docker.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh
EOF_DMS_CERTSVC
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.timer <<'EOF_DMS_CERTTIMER'
[Unit]
Description=Periodic Caddy to Docker Mailserver TLS certificate sync
[Timer]
OnActiveSec=5min
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
Persistent=true
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF_DMS_CERTTIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh || true

# First mailbox and DKIM keys. Nothing here is fatal and no output
# is discarded — the same rule the mailcow API, the Nextcloud occ
# and the Mailu CLI blocks follow: errexit in the middle of this
# step would take the remaining services and the revocation of the
# install key with it, and a mailbox is addable afterwards.
DMS_OUT=""
dms_exec() { DMS_OUT="$(timeout 120 docker exec mailserver "$@" 2>&1)"; }
# Passwords go in on stdin, never in argv: the arguments of
# `docker exec` are readable out of /proc by every account on the
# box. The helper asks for the password twice, so it is fed twice.
# $1 add|update, $2 address, $3 password.
dms_mailbox() {
  DMS_OUT="$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$3" "$3" \
    | timeout 120 docker exec -i mailserver setup email "$1" "$2" 2>&1)"
}
dms_why() { printf '%s' "$DMS_OUT" | tr -d '\r\n' | cut -c1-300; }
# A deadline, not a number of tries: each attempt can burn its own
# timeout, so counting attempts leaves the real wait unbounded.
# The probe is `setup help` and NOT `setup email list`: the list
# subcommand exits 1 while no account exists — which is exactly the
# state of every fresh install — so it answered "not ready" until
# the deadline ran out and neither the first mailbox nor the DKIM
# keys were ever created.
DMS_READY=0
DMS_TRY=0
DMS_DEADLINE=$(($(date +%s) + 300))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$DMS_DEADLINE" ]; do
  if dms_exec setup help; then DMS_READY=1; break; fi
  DMS_TRY=$((DMS_TRY + 1))
  # Heartbeat every ~30 s: silence here is indistinguishable from a
  # hung install in the app's progress view.
  if [ "$((DMS_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Docker Mailserver: waiting for the container to finish its own setup ($(dms_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$DMS_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  DMS_PASSWORD="$(grep '^FIRST_MAILBOX_PASSWORD=' /opt/docker-mailserver/.env | cut -d= -f2- || true)"
  # Its failure IS the answer "there are no accounts yet" — the
  # account file does not exist until the first one is added — so
  # it must not take the step down with it under errexit.
  dms_exec setup email list || true
  # `email list` prints one line per mailbox; matching the address
  # at a word boundary keeps a lookalike account from passing for
  # this one and silently skipping creation — the Forgejo lesson.
  if ! printf '%s' "$DMS_OUT" | grep -qE "(^|[[:space:]*])admin@example.com([[:space:]]|$)"; then
    if [ -n "$DMS_PASSWORD" ]; then
      dms_mailbox add "admin@example.com" "$DMS_PASSWORD" \
        || log "Docker Mailserver: the first mailbox was NOT created. The server is running: add it from the app, or with 'setup email add' on the server. ($(dms_why))"
    fi
  fi
    # Idempotent: the helper skips a domain that already has a key.
  # The selector is spelled out — the default is `mail`, and the
  # DNS artifact tells the user to publish `dkim._domainkey`.
  dms_exec setup config dkim keysize 2048 selector dkim domain example.com \
    || log "Docker Mailserver: could not create the DKIM key for example.com — add it later from the server ($(dms_why))"
  # Idempotent: the helper skips a domain that already has a key.
  # The selector is spelled out — the default is `mail`, and the
  # DNS artifact tells the user to publish `dkim._domainkey`.
  dms_exec setup config dkim keysize 2048 selector dkim domain example.org \
    || log "Docker Mailserver: could not create the DKIM key for example.org — add it later from the server ($(dms_why))"
  # rspamd looks the signing key up under the eSLD unless told not to,
  # so a mail domain that is a SUBDOMAIN never matches its own key and
  # goes out unsigned. Our keys are filed under the exact domain.
  DMS_DKIM_CONF="/opt/docker-mailserver/config/rspamd/override.d/dkim_signing.conf"
  if [ -f "$DMS_DKIM_CONF" ] && grep -q '^use_esld = true;' "$DMS_DKIM_CONF"; then
    sed -i 's/^use_esld = true;/use_esld = false;/' "$DMS_DKIM_CONF"
    # rspamd reads this at start; without the restart the fix applies
    # only after the next unrelated container restart.
    dms_exec supervisorctl restart rspamd || true
  fi
else
  log "Docker Mailserver did not finish its setup in time — no mailbox and no DKIM keys were created; check the container logs ($(dms_why))"
fi

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-mailbox.sh <<'EOF_DMS_MAILBOX'
#!/bin/bash
# Mailbox management for the gryonixNexus dashboard.
# Usage: gryonixnexus-dms-mailbox.sh list
#        gryonixnexus-dms-mailbox.sh add <address> (password on stdin)
#        gryonixnexus-dms-mailbox.sh del <address>
#        gryonixnexus-dms-mailbox.sh password <address> (password on stdin)
set -euo pipefail
cd /opt/docker-mailserver 2>/dev/null || { echo "docker mailserver is not installed" >&2; exit 2; }
ACTION="${1:-}"
ADDRESS="${2:-}"
# The address is checked HERE, not by the container: this script runs as
# root through sudo, so an argument that reaches `docker exec` unchecked
# is an argument that reaches root. One local part, one domain, no
# shell metacharacters, no leading dash that could read as a flag.
check_address() {
  case "$ADDRESS" in
    -*|*[!a-zA-Z0-9.@_+-]*|*@*@*|@*|*@) echo "invalid address: ${ADDRESS}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *@*) ;;
    *) echo "invalid address: ${ADDRESS}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
}
# The password arrives on stdin, never in argv, where /proc would show
# it to every account on the box.
read_password() {
  if [ -t 0 ]; then echo "a password is required on stdin" >&2; exit 2; fi
  PASSWORD="$(cat)"
  [ -n "$PASSWORD" ] || { echo "the password is empty" >&2; exit 2; }
}
case "$ACTION" in
  list)
    # An install with no mailboxes yet is an EMPTY LIST, not a failure:
    # `setup email list` exits 1 for as long as the account file does
    # not exist, and the app would show an error where it should show
    # "no mailboxes". The file is checked on the host — it is the same
    # directory the container has mounted, so this adds no second
    # source of truth. A container that is down still makes the listing
    # fail, which the app does need to see.
    if [ -s /opt/docker-mailserver/config/postfix-accounts.cf ]; then
      docker exec mailserver setup email list
    fi
    ;;
  add)
    check_address; read_password
    # The password goes down stdin into the container as well, not as
    # an argument: `docker exec` argv is world-readable in /proc. The
    # helper prompts for it twice, hence the two lines.
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$PASSWORD" "$PASSWORD" \
      | docker exec -i mailserver setup email add "$ADDRESS" >/dev/null
    echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_MAILBOX_DONE add ${ADDRESS}"
    ;;
  del)
    check_address
    # Retried, because deleting a mailbox seconds after creating it
    # loses a race INSIDE the engine: `addmailuser` writes the account
    # line at once, but the mail directory is created asynchronously
    # about a second later, and `delmailuser` refuses while it is not
    # there ("Mailbox data directory … does not exist"). Absent at t=0, present at t=1s, and the very same
    # call then succeeds. Nothing is destroyed by the refusal — the
    # account line survives — so retrying is safe, and "add a mailbox,
    # notice the typo, delete it" is the most likely first thing
    # anyone does with this screen.
    # The LAST attempt runs with its output visible: whatever is
    # really wrong, the engine's own words are the only explanation
    # the app can show, and the marker is not printed on failure.
    DEL_TRY=1
    while true; do
      if [ "$DEL_TRY" -ge 5 ]; then
        docker exec mailserver setup email del -y "$ADDRESS" >/dev/null
        break
      fi
      if docker exec mailserver setup email del -y "$ADDRESS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        break
      fi
      DEL_TRY=$((DEL_TRY + 1))
      sleep 2
    done
    echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_MAILBOX_DONE del ${ADDRESS}"
    ;;
  password)
    check_address; read_password
    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$PASSWORD" "$PASSWORD" \
      | docker exec -i mailserver setup email update "$ADDRESS" >/dev/null
    echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_MAILBOX_DONE password ${ADDRESS}"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "unsupported action: ${ACTION}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
EOF_DMS_MAILBOX
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-mailbox.sh
cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-dkim.sh <<'EOF_DMS_DKIM'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# `setup config dkim` is what actually MINTS the key (see the install
# step that calls it), and it always writes BIND-format keys under
# opendkim/keys/<domain>/dkim.txt — REGARDLESS of ENABLE_RSPAMD vs
# ENABLE_OPENDKIM. Rspamd's dkim_signing module reads its signing key
# from that same path by the image's own default config; "opendkim"
# here names where the key lives, not which engine signs with it.
#
# An earlier version of this wrapper globbed
# `rspamd/dkim/*-dkim-*.public.dns.txt`, a path rspamd never writes on
# this image: the real
# key sat at opendkim/keys/<domain>/dkim.txt the whole time, and the
# glob matched nothing, so every report said "not ready yet" forever.
#
# dkim.txt is a BIND zone-file record, not a bare value:
#   dkim._domainkey IN TXT ( "v=DKIM1; h=sha256; k=rsa; "
#     "p=MIIB..." "dYRV...AB" )  ; ----- DKIM key dkim for <domain>
# The quoted segments concatenate directly (no separator) into the
# single value to publish — the first segment's own trailing space
# is what keeps "k=rsa;" and "p=..." apart, so no extra space is added
# here.
for F in /opt/docker-mailserver/config/opendkim/keys/*/dkim.txt; do
  [ -f "$F" ] || continue
  D="$(basename "$(dirname "$F")")"
  V="$(grep -o '"[^"]*"' "$F" | tr -d '"\n' | head -c 2000)"
  [ -n "$V" ] || continue
  # Bare, no quotes around $V — mailcow and Mailu both print the value
  # unquoted (see their own dkimMarker lines), and DKIMRecordParser /
  # DKIMExport downstream both expect the bare "v=DKIM1;...;p=..."
  # string, adding their own quoting where a format needs it (the BIND
  # zone export, the DNS provider's own form). A quoted value here
  # would ship the literal `"` characters into every artifact and
  # clipboard copy built from it.
  echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM dkim._domainkey.$D $V"
done
echo "GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM_DONE"
EOF_DMS_DKIM
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-dkim.sh
reportSteps:
echo "Docker Mailserver:"
echo "  Webmail:     https://mail.example.com"
echo "  First mailbox: admin@example.com"
echo "  Password (generated on the server): $(grep '^FIRST_MAILBOX_PASSWORD=' /opt/docker-mailserver/.env | cut -d= -f2-)"
echo "  Further mailboxes are added from the app — this engine has no web admin of its own"
echo "  DKIM records (add them to DNS):"
/opt/gryonixnexus-dms-dkim.sh 2>/dev/null | grep '^GRYONIXNEXUS_DKIM ' | while read -r _ NAME VALUE; do
  echo "    $NAME TXT $VALUE"
done || echo "    not ready yet — run the DKIM setup again on the server"
setupSteps:
log "Docker Mailserver: starting"
install -d -m 755 /opt/docker-mailserver /opt/docker-mailserver/mail-data /opt/docker-mailserver/mail-state /opt/docker-mailserver/mail-logs /opt/docker-mailserver/config /opt/docker-mailserver/webmail /opt/docker-mailserver/webmail-db
# The certificate directory is root-only: the container reads it
# read-only, and nothing else on the host has business there.
install -d -m 700 /opt/docker-mailserver/certs
# SSL_TYPE=manual does NOT degrade when the files are missing: the
# engine prints "File … does not exist!", shuts down, and
# `restart: unless-stopped` turns that into a permanent crash
# loop. Caddy only obtains the real certificate two steps later,
# so on a fresh install there is nothing to point at yet — and a
# container stuck in that loop never gets its first mailbox or its
# DKIM keys either. A self-signed placeholder lets the engine boot;
# the sync below replaces it the moment Caddy has the real one.
# Live-found: without this the whole engine never starts.
if [ ! -s /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/cert.pem ] || [ ! -s /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/key.pem ]; then
  if openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 3650 \
       -subj "/CN=mail.example.com" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:mail.example.com" \
       -keyout /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/key.pem -out /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/cert.pem >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chmod 644 /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/cert.pem
    chmod 600 /opt/docker-mailserver/certs/key.pem
  else
    log "Docker Mailserver: could not create the temporary certificate — the mail container will not start until the real certificate arrives"
  fi
fi
cd /opt/docker-mailserver
docker compose -p dockermailserver pull -q
docker compose -p dockermailserver up -d

cat > /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh <<'EOF_DMS_CERTSYNC'
#!/bin/bash
set -eu
DOMAIN="mail.example.com"
DMS="/opt/docker-mailserver"
DEST="$DMS/certs"
CADDY_DATA="/var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates"
SRC_CRT="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.crt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
SRC_KEY="$(find "$CADDY_DATA" -type f -name "${DOMAIN}.key" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
# No certificate yet (ACME still pending) is not an error: the timer
# comes back every hour and the mail ports keep serving what they have.
if [ -z "$SRC_CRT" ] || [ -z "$SRC_KEY" ]; then exit 0; fi
if cmp -s "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem" && cmp -s "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"; then exit 0; fi
cp "$SRC_CRT" "$DEST/cert.pem"
cp "$SRC_KEY" "$DEST/key.pem"
chmod 644 "$DEST/cert.pem"
chmod 600 "$DEST/key.pem"
cd "$DMS"
# Postfix and Dovecot read the certificate at start; the container has
# no reload hook for a file that changed under it.
docker compose -p dockermailserver restart mailserver >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
EOF_DMS_CERTSYNC
chmod 700 /opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.service <<'EOF_DMS_CERTSVC'
[Unit]
Description=Sync Caddy TLS certificate into Docker Mailserver (SMTP/IMAPS)
After=docker.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh
EOF_DMS_CERTSVC
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.timer <<'EOF_DMS_CERTTIMER'
[Unit]
Description=Periodic Caddy to Docker Mailserver TLS certificate sync
[Timer]
OnActiveSec=5min
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
Persistent=true
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF_DMS_CERTTIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/opt/gryonixnexus-dms-cert-sync.sh || true

# First mailbox and DKIM keys. Nothing here is fatal and no output
# is discarded — the same rule the mailcow API, the Nextcloud occ
# and the Mailu CLI blocks follow: errexit in the middle of this
# step would take the remaining services and the revocation of the
# install key with it, and a mailbox is addable afterwards.
DMS_OUT=""
dms_exec() { DMS_OUT="$(timeout 120 docker exec mailserver "$@" 2>&1)"; }
# Passwords go in on stdin, never in argv: the arguments of
# `docker exec` are readable out of /proc by every account on the
# box. The helper asks for the password twice, so it is fed twice.
# $1 add|update, $2 address, $3 password.
dms_mailbox() {
  DMS_OUT="$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$3" "$3" \
    | timeout 120 docker exec -i mailserver setup email "$1" "$2" 2>&1)"
}
dms_why() { printf '%s' "$DMS_OUT" | tr -d '\r\n' | cut -c1-300; }
# A deadline, not a number of tries: each attempt can burn its own
# timeout, so counting attempts leaves the real wait unbounded.
# The probe is `setup help` and NOT `setup email list`: the list
# subcommand exits 1 while no account exists — which is exactly the
# state of every fresh install — so it answered "not ready" until
# the deadline ran out and neither the first mailbox nor the DKIM
# keys were ever created.
DMS_READY=0
DMS_TRY=0
DMS_DEADLINE=$(($(date +%s) + 300))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$DMS_DEADLINE" ]; do
  if dms_exec setup help; then DMS_READY=1; break; fi
  DMS_TRY=$((DMS_TRY + 1))
  # Heartbeat every ~30 s: silence here is indistinguishable from a
  # hung install in the app's progress view.
  if [ "$((DMS_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Docker Mailserver: waiting for the container to finish its own setup ($(dms_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$DMS_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  DMS_PASSWORD="$(grep '^FIRST_MAILBOX_PASSWORD=' /opt/docker-mailserver/.env | cut -d= -f2- || true)"
  # Its failure IS the answer "there are no accounts yet" — the
  # account file does not exist until the first one is added — so
  # it must not take the step down with it under errexit.
  dms_exec setup email list || true
  # `email list` prints one line per mailbox; matching the address
  # at a word boundary keeps a lookalike account from passing for
  # this one and silently skipping creation — the Forgejo lesson.
  if ! printf '%s' "$DMS_OUT" | grep -qE "(^|[[:space:]*])admin@example.com([[:space:]]|$)"; then
    if [ -n "$DMS_PASSWORD" ]; then
      dms_mailbox add "admin@example.com" "$DMS_PASSWORD" \
        || log "Docker Mailserver: the first mailbox was NOT created. The server is running: add it from the app, or with 'setup email add' on the server. ($(dms_why))"
    fi
  fi
    # Idempotent: the helper skips a domain that already has a key.
  # The selector is spelled out — the default is `mail`, and the
  # DNS artifact tells the user to publish `dkim._domainkey`.
  dms_exec setup config dkim keysize 2048 selector dkim domain example.com \
    || log "Docker Mailserver: could not create the DKIM key for example.com — add it later from the server ($(dms_why))"
  # Idempotent: the helper skips a domain that already has a key.
  # The selector is spelled out — the default is `mail`, and the
  # DNS artifact tells the user to publish `dkim._domainkey`.
  dms_exec setup config dkim keysize 2048 selector dkim domain example.org \
    || log "Docker Mailserver: could not create the DKIM key for example.org — add it later from the server ($(dms_why))"
  # rspamd looks the signing key up under the eSLD unless told not to,
  # so a mail domain that is a SUBDOMAIN never matches its own key and
  # goes out unsigned. Our keys are filed under the exact domain.
  DMS_DKIM_CONF="/opt/docker-mailserver/config/rspamd/override.d/dkim_signing.conf"
  if [ -f "$DMS_DKIM_CONF" ] && grep -q '^use_esld = true;' "$DMS_DKIM_CONF"; then
    sed -i 's/^use_esld = true;/use_esld = false;/' "$DMS_DKIM_CONF"
    # rspamd reads this at start; without the restart the fix applies
    # only after the next unrelated container restart.
    dms_exec supervisorctl restart rspamd || true
  fi
else
  log "Docker Mailserver did not finish its setup in time — no mailbox and no DKIM keys were created; check the container logs ($(dms_why))"
fi

internalTLSComposeContents:
services:
  vaultwarden:
    image: vaultwarden/server:latest
    container_name: vaultwarden
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DOMAIN: "https://vaultwarden.example.com"
      SIGNUPS_ALLOWED: "false"
      ADMIN_TOKEN: ${ADMIN_TOKEN}
      IP_HEADER: X-Forwarded-For
    volumes:
      - /opt/vaultwarden/data:/data
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8082:80"
internalTLSSetupSteps:
log "Vaultwarden: starting"
cd /opt/vaultwarden
VW_CONFIG="/opt/vaultwarden/data/config.json"
VW_DOMAIN="https://vaultwarden.example.com"
VW_RESTART=0
if [ -f "$VW_CONFIG" ]; then
  # The stored domain is only compared when the key is present: absent
  # means the compose environment still rules and needs no rewrite. When
  # it IS present it outranks env, so a reinstall onto another domain
  # would keep serving links to the old one.
  if ! jq -e --arg d "$VW_DOMAIN" \
       '.signups_allowed == false and ((.domain // $d) == $d)' \
       "$VW_CONFIG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    VW_TMP="$(mktemp)"
    jq --arg d "$VW_DOMAIN" \
       '.signups_allowed = false | if has("domain") then .domain = $d else . end' \
       "$VW_CONFIG" > "$VW_TMP"
    mv "$VW_TMP" "$VW_CONFIG"
    chmod 600 "$VW_CONFIG"
    VW_RESTART=1
  fi
fi
docker compose -p vaultwarden pull -q
docker compose -p vaultwarden up -d
if [ "$VW_RESTART" = "1" ]; then
  docker restart vaultwarden
fi

echo "Vaultwarden:  https://vaultwarden.example.com"
echo "  Admin panel: https://vaultwarden.example.com/admin"
echo "  Admin token (generated on the server): $(grep '^ADMIN_TOKEN=' /opt/vaultwarden/.env | cut -d= -f2-)"
echo "  Sign-in: open the URL and create your own account (your email + a master password you choose). The admin token above is only for the /admin panel."
echo "  Signups: closed — invite users from the admin panel"
setupSteps:
log "Vaultwarden: starting"
cd /opt/vaultwarden
VW_CONFIG="/opt/vaultwarden/data/config.json"
VW_DOMAIN="https://vaultwarden.example.com"
VW_RESTART=0
if [ -f "$VW_CONFIG" ]; then
  # The stored domain is only compared when the key is present: absent
  # means the compose environment still rules and needs no rewrite. When
  # it IS present it outranks env, so a reinstall onto another domain
  # would keep serving links to the old one.
  if ! jq -e --arg d "$VW_DOMAIN" \
       '.signups_allowed == false and ((.domain // $d) == $d)' \
       "$VW_CONFIG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    VW_TMP="$(mktemp)"
    jq --arg d "$VW_DOMAIN" \
       '.signups_allowed = false | if has("domain") then .domain = $d else . end' \
       "$VW_CONFIG" > "$VW_TMP"
    mv "$VW_TMP" "$VW_CONFIG"
    chmod 600 "$VW_CONFIG"
    VW_RESTART=1
  fi
fi
docker compose -p vaultwarden pull -q
docker compose -p vaultwarden up -d
if [ "$VW_RESTART" = "1" ]; then
  docker restart vaultwarden
fi

restart	restart	sudo docker compose -p psono restart
start	restart	sudo docker compose -p psono start
stop	restart	sudo docker compose -p psono stop
logs	quick	sudo docker compose -p psono logs --tail 500 --timestamps
backup	long	sudo /opt/gryonixnexus-backup-ctl.sh

composeContents:
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      # Read by the shared backup wrapper from the container's OWN
      # environment — compose already put it there — because
      # passing it from the host would sit in the argv of docker
      # exec, where /proc hands it to every account.
      POSTGRES_DB: psono
      POSTGRES_USER: psono
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${PSONO_DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - /opt/psono/db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
  psono:
    image: psono/psono-combo:7.3.0-4.7.2-1.8.2
    container_name: psono
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - db
    # Upstream's own installation guide sets this on the combo
    # container; left at the kernel default, a busy instance drops
    # connections under load rather than queuing them.
    sysctls:
      net.core.somaxconn: 65535
    volumes:
      # settings.yaml is written by setupSteps below, not by this
      # compose file — it is not env-templated (see the type
      # comment: two of its keys are a matched keypair). The same
      # config.json is mounted twice, into the web client AND the
      # admin portal, exactly as Psono's own reference compose
      # does — they are two apps served by the same nginx and read
      # the same "which server do I talk to" file.
      - /opt/psono/config/settings.yaml:/root/.psono_server/settings.yaml
      - /opt/psono/config/webclient/config.json:/usr/share/nginx/html/config.json
      - /opt/psono/config/webclient/config.json:/usr/share/nginx/html/portal/config.json
    ports:
      # The combo image runs its OWN nginx on 80 in front of the
      # web client, the admin portal AND the Django server (at
      # /server) — one upstream port covers all three, and Caddy
      # speaks plain HTTP to it like every other service here.
      - "127.0.0.1:8089:80"

internalTLSSetupSteps:

install -d -m 755 /opt/psono/db /opt/psono/config /opt/psono/config/webclient
# The web client and the admin portal read the SAME file to learn
# which server to talk to — see the compose double-mount above.
# allow_custom_server is off: nobody should be able to point this
# client at a different backend from the login screen.
cat > /opt/psono/config/webclient/config.json <<EOF_PS_CLIENT
{
  "backend_servers": [{"title": "Psono", "url": "https://psono.example.com/server"}],
  "base_url": "https://psono.example.com/",
  "allow_custom_server": false,
  "allow_registration": false,
  "allow_lost_password": false,
  "disable_download_bar": false,
  "remember_me_default": false,
  "trust_device_default": false,
  "authentication_methods": ["AUTHKEY"],
  "saml_provider": []
}
EOF_PS_CLIENT

# settings.yaml is generated ONCE. `generateserverkeys.py` prints
# SECRET_KEY / ACTIVATION_LINK_SECRET / DB_SECRET / EMAIL_SECRET_SALT
# (independent random values) AND PRIVATE_KEY / PUBLIC_KEY — a
# matched Curve25519 pair the image derives with nacl, which is
# exactly why they are not __RANDOM__ envTemplate lines: two
# independently random hex strings would not be a valid keypair.
# Its stdout IS already valid YAML (Python repr()-quoted), so it is
# captured straight into the file with no re-quoting on this side.
# Guarded by file existence, the same idempotency rule as every
# other first-run secret in this catalog — a re-run (repair,
# reinstall onto the same path) must never regenerate keys that
# existing encrypted datastores already depend on.
PS_FRESH=0
if [ ! -f /opt/psono/config/settings.yaml ]; then
  PS_FRESH=1
  docker run --rm psono/psono-combo:7.3.0-4.7.2-1.8.2 python3 ./psono/generateserverkeys.py > /opt/psono/config/settings.yaml
  PS_DB_PASSWORD="$(grep '^PSONO_DB_PASSWORD=' /opt/psono/.env | cut -d= -f2-)"

  # is closed from this first write, never opened later — an
  # instance that was briefly open is a window this catalog does
  # not accept for any service (Forgejo's INSTALL_LOCK is the same
  # rule). The favicon service defaults to a THIRD PARTY endpoint
  # (Psono's own privacy-friendly proxy, or Google's) that the
  # client calls per stored URL to fetch an icon — left blank so
  # nothing here calls out on its own.
  cat >> /opt/psono/config/settings.yaml <<EOF_PS_SETTINGS
WEB_CLIENT_URL: 'https://psono.example.com'
HOST_URL: 'https://psono.example.com/server'
# Two hops in front of the Django app: Caddy, then the combo
# image's own nginx. Psono's own docs name this exact number for
# this exact topology.
NUM_PROXIES: 2
ALLOWED_HOSTS: ['*']
ALLOWED_DOMAINS: ['example.com']
ALLOW_REGISTRATION: False
ALLOW_LOST_PASSWORD: False
MANAGEMENT_ENABLED: True
DEBUG: False
FAVICON_SERVICE_URL: ''
EMAIL_FROM: 'psono@example.com'
EMAIL_HOST: ''
EMAIL_HOST_USER: ''
EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD: ''
EMAIL_PORT: 25
EMAIL_USE_TLS: False
EMAIL_USE_SSL: False
DATABASES:
  default:
    'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.postgresql_psycopg2'
    'NAME': 'psono'
    'USER': 'psono'
    'PASSWORD': '$PS_DB_PASSWORD'
    'HOST': 'db'
    'PORT': '5432'
EOF_PS_SETTINGS
  chmod 600 /opt/psono/config/settings.yaml
fi
cd /opt/psono
docker compose -p psono pull -q
docker compose -p psono up -d

# `presetup` installs the ltree/pgcrypto extensions Psono needs and
# `migrate` applies the schema — both idempotent, so both run on
# EVERY setup pass, not only a fresh install: this catalog's other
# services update by pulling a new image and restarting alone,
# which would silently skip a migration a new Psono version needs.
#
# Nothing below is fatal and no output is discarded: the same rule
# the mailcow API, Nextcloud occ, Forgejo and Seafile provisioning
# blocks follow. This sits in the middle of a `set -euo pipefail`
# script whose remaining steps include revoking the install key.
PS_OUT=""
ps_exec() { PS_OUT="$(timeout 60 docker exec psono "$@" 2>&1)"; }
ps_why() { printf '%s' "$PS_OUT" | tr -d '\r\n' | cut -c1-300; }
# A deadline, not a number of tries: each attempt can burn its own
# timeout. `presetup` doubles as the readiness probe — it needs a
# working database connection, which is the thing not ready yet
# while the container already reports up.
PS_READY=0
PS_TRY=0
PS_DEADLINE=$(($(date +%s) + 300))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$PS_DEADLINE" ]; do
  if ps_exec python3 ./psono/manage.py presetup; then PS_READY=1; break; fi
  PS_TRY=$((PS_TRY + 1))
  if [ "$((PS_TRY % 6))" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "Psono: waiting for the database to become reachable ($(ps_why))"
  fi
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$PS_READY" -eq 1 ]; then
  ps_exec python3 ./psono/manage.py migrate || log "Psono: could not apply database migrations — run them manually inside the container (manage.py migrate) ($(ps_why))"
  if [ "$PS_FRESH" -eq 1 ]; then
    PS_ADMIN_PASSWORD="$(grep '^PSONO_ADMIN_PASSWORD=' /opt/psono/.env | cut -d= -f2- || true)"
    if [ -n "$PS_ADMIN_PASSWORD" ]; then
      ps_exec python3 ./psono/manage.py createuser admin@example.com "$PS_ADMIN_PASSWORD" admin@example.com \
        && ps_exec python3 ./psono/manage.py promoteuser admin@example.com superuser \
        && ps_exec python3 ./psono/manage.py verifyuseremail admin@example.com \
        || log "Psono: could not create the administrator account — create one manually inside the container (manage.py createuser, then promoteuser) ($(ps_why))"
    fi
  fi
else
  log "Psono did not become reachable in time — the administrator account was not created; re-run the setup or create it manually ($(ps_why))"
fi

composeContents:
services:
  db:
    image: mariadb:10.11
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      # Explicit, NOT upstream's own MYSQL_RANDOM_ROOT_PASSWORD:
      # the shared backup wrapper always dumps as root, reading
      # MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD out of the container's OWN
      # environment — a randomized-and-discarded root password
      # would make this service's own backups impossible.
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${PASSBOLT_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
      MYSQL_DATABASE: passbolt
      MYSQL_USER: passbolt
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${PASSBOLT_DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - /opt/passbolt/db:/var/lib/mysql
  passbolt:
    image: passbolt/passbolt:5.14.3-1-ce
    container_name: passbolt
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - db
    environment:
      APP_FULL_BASE_URL: https://passbolt.example.com
      DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_HOST: db
      DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_USERNAME: passbolt
      DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_PASSWORD: ${PASSBOLT_DB_PASSWORD}
      DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_DATABASE: passbolt
    volumes:
      - /opt/passbolt/secrets/gpg:/etc/passbolt/gpg
      - /opt/passbolt/secrets/jwt:/etc/passbolt/jwt
    # `depends_on` only waits for the db CONTAINER to start, not
    # for MariaDB to accept connections — this is upstream's own
    # wait, kept verbatim, ahead of the entrypoint that generates
    # the GPG keypair and installs the schema.
    command:
      [
        "/usr/bin/wait-for.sh",
        "-t",
        "0",
        "db:3306",
        "--",
        "/docker-entrypoint.sh",
      ]
    ports:
      # Caddy terminates TLS and speaks plain HTTP to this port —
      # the community has documented this exact shape (nginx or
      # Caddy in front on 80, Passbolt never sees the TLS layer);
      # unlike mailcow's nginx, nothing here redirects 80 to 443
      # on its own. Port 443 is never published: this catalog's
      # own self-signed listener has no certificate anyone trusts
      # and Caddy already owns the public 443.
      - "127.0.0.1:8090:80"

internalTLSSetupSteps:
log "Passbolt: starting"
install -d -m 755 /opt/passbolt/db
# The two secret directories are NOT 755 root:root like every other
# directory here, and the difference is what makes the service start
# at all. The image ships /etc/passbolt/gpg as root:www-data 0770 and
# /etc/passbolt/jwt as root:www-data 0750, and the server drops to
# www-data to write the GPG keypair it generates on first boot.
# Upstream's own compose mounts NAMED volumes there, which docker
# seeds with the image's ownership and mode; a BIND mount is never
# seeded, so the container sees the host directory's own root:root
# 0755 and cannot write. The server
# crash-looped on "/etc/passbolt/gpg/serverkey_private.asc:
# Permission denied", restarting every few seconds forever.
# Bind mounts are not negotiable — the backup wrapper archives
# /opt/passbolt, so the keys have to sit on a real host path.
# The group is the NUMBER 33, not the name: it has to match the uid
# map inside the container, and nothing guarantees the host even has
# a www-data group, let alone at the same id.
install -d -m 770 -o root -g 33 /opt/passbolt/secrets/gpg
install -d -m 750 -o root -g 33 /opt/passbolt/secrets/jwt

# earlier run already sent the one-time admin invitation — the
# entrypoint generates that key exactly once, on its very first
# start, and this service piggybacks on that same signal so a
# repair/reinstall over the same volumes never re-invites (the
# first invitation may already be used, and inviting a duplicate
# "admin" the CLI would refuse anyway).
PB_FRESH=0
[ -f /opt/passbolt/secrets/gpg/serverkey_private.asc ] || PB_FRESH=1
cd /opt/passbolt
docker compose -p passbolt pull -q
docker compose -p passbolt up -d

pb_exec() { PB_OUT="$(timeout 60 docker exec passbolt "$@" 2>&1)"; }

docker compose -p nextcloud pull -q

cd /opt/nextcloud
# Nextcloud writes trusted_domains/overwritehost into config.php only
# when it FIRST initialises the instance; the compose environment is
# ignored afterwards. A reinstall onto another domain would therefore
# be met with "Access through untrusted domain". Re-apply the
# current hostname on every run — a no-op when it already matches.
NC_APP="$(docker compose -p nextcloud ps -q app 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
if [ -n "$NC_APP" ]; then
  # occ's output is CAPTURED, never discarded, and no call here is
  # fatal — the same rule the mailcow API block follows. This ran
  # `occ … >/dev/null 2>&1` outside any `if`, so a freshly started
  # instance that answered `status` but was not ready for
  # config:system:set killed the whole install through errexit: on
  # a real run it died at step 9 of 22 with exit 1 and NOT ONE line
  # of explanation, leaving a half-configured server. A trusted
  # domain can be fixed from the admin UI; a half-install cannot.
  NC_OUT=""
  nc_occ() { NC_OUT="$(docker exec -u www-data "$NC_APP" php occ "$@" 2>&1)"; }
  # Why the last call failed, bounded to one line: occ can answer
  # with a stack trace, and the app streams this log.
  nc_why() { printf '%s' "$NC_OUT" | tr -d '\r\n' | cut -c1-300; }
  # **`occ status` EXITS 0 on an instance that is not installed,
  # and reading its status as readiness is why every setting below
  # was lost.** On a fresh container it answers
  # "Nextcloud is not installed - only a limited number of commands
  # are available" and returns success, so the wait broke out on
  # its very first try and every `config:system:set` after it died
  # with "There are no commands defined in the config:system
  # namespace". The visible cost was an instance left on the
  # image's own `overwrite.cli.url` — https://localhost — with the
  # log carrying three failures nobody could act on. The ANSWER is what has to be read, not
  # the status: `installed: true` is printed only once the
  # installer has finished.
  nc_ready() {
    nc_occ status || return 1
    printf '%s' "$NC_OUT" | grep -q 'installed: true'
  }
  for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    nc_ready && break
    sleep 5
  done
  if nc_ready; then
    # Index 1, never 0: slot 0 holds "localhost" from the image's own
    # installer and dropping it would cut local access off.
    # One slot per name the Caddy site serves — the alias domains
    # included, or Nextcloud answers them "untrusted domain" while
    # Caddy happily holds a certificate for them.
    nc_occ config:system:set trusted_domains 1 --value=nextcloud.example.com \
      || log "Nextcloud: could not set trusted_domains 1 — set it under Administration settings or in config.php. ($(nc_why))"
    nc_occ config:system:set trusted_domains 2 --value=nextcloud.example.org \
      || log "Nextcloud: could not set trusted_domains 2 — set it under Administration settings or in config.php. ($(nc_why))"
    nc_occ config:system:set trusted_domains 3 --value='*' \
      || log "Nextcloud: could not set trusted_domains 3 — set it under Administration settings or in config.php. ($(nc_why))"
    nc_occ config:system:delete overwritehost
    nc_occ config:system:delete overwriteprotocol
    nc_occ config:system:set overwrite.cli.url --value=https://nextcloud.example.com \
      || log "Nextcloud: could not set overwrite.cli.url — set it under Administration settings or in config.php. ($(nc_why))"

      || log "Nextcloud: could not set maintenance_window_start — set it under Administration settings or in config.php. ($(nc_why))"
    nc_occ background:cron \
      || log "Nextcloud: could not set background:cron — set it under Administration settings or in config.php. ($(nc_why))"
    nc_occ db:add-missing-indices \
      || log "Nextcloud: could not set db:add-missing-indices — set it under Administration settings or in config.php. ($(nc_why))"
    nc_occ maintenance:repair --include-expensive \

  fi

composeContents:
services:
  db:
    image: mariadb:10.11
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      # The shared backup wrapper dumps through this variable, read
      # out of the container's OWN environment — a password passed
      # from the host would sit in the argv of docker exec, where
      # /proc hands it to every account. There is deliberately no
      # MYSQL_DATABASE: Seafile owns three, and the backup plan
      # names each one instead.
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${SEAFILE_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
      MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE: "1"
    volumes:
      - /opt/seafile/db:/var/lib/mysql
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Cache only, so persistence is off: an appendonly file here
    # would be disk traffic for data that is rebuilt on demand.
    # No password either — redis takes it as a command-line
    # argument, which puts it in the process table where the host
    # can read it, and it buys nothing over a port that is never
    # published outside this project's own network.
    command: ["redis-server", "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no"]
  seafile:
    image: seafileltd/seafile-mc:13.0.25
    container_name: seafile
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - db
      - redis
    environment:
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_HOST: db
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_PORT: "3306"
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_USER: seafile
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_PASSWORD: ${SEAFILE_DB_PASSWORD}
      # Only used on the first start, to create the three schemas
      # and the unprivileged user above.
      INIT_SEAFILE_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${SEAFILE_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_CCNET_DB_NAME: ccnet_db
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_SEAFILE_DB_NAME: seafile_db
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_SEAHUB_DB_NAME: seahub_db
      # The administrator, created on the first start. Left unset,
      # Seafile creates me@example.com with the password `asecret`
      # — a documented credential on a public hostname.
      INIT_SEAFILE_ADMIN_EMAIL: admin@example.com
      INIT_SEAFILE_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${SEAFILE_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      # SERVICE_URL and FILE_SERVER_ROOT are derived from these two
      # on every start, so they stay SINGLE-valued at the canonical
      # name even though the Caddy site answers on the aliases too.
      # The protocol must be https: it is what the browser speaks,
      # and an http value here makes every download link a
      # mixed-content block.
      SEAFILE_SERVER_HOSTNAME: seafile.example.com
      SEAFILE_SERVER_PROTOCOL: https
      SITE_ROOT: /
      NON_ROOT: "false"
      TIME_ZONE: Etc/UTC
      JWT_PRIVATE_KEY: ${SEAFILE_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY}
      # SeaDoc is a SEPARATE container upstream ships in its own
      # compose file. Left at its default (true) the server
      # advertises a /sdoc-server endpoint that nothing answers, so
      # opening a document fails with no explanation — off is the
      # honest state of an install that does not include it.
      ENABLE_SEADOC: "false"
      CACHE_PROVIDER: redis
      REDIS_HOST: redis
      REDIS_PORT: "6379"
    volumes:
      - /opt/seafile/data:/shared
    ports:
      # The container runs its own nginx on 80, which fronts
      # seahub, the file server and WebDAV on one port.
      - "127.0.0.1:8088:80"

      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_CCNET_DB_NAME: ccnet_db
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_SEAFILE_DB_NAME: seafile_db
      SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_SEAHUB_DB_NAME: seahub_db

      # Seafile creates me@example.com with the password `asecret`

      INIT_SEAFILE_ADMIN_EMAIL: admin@example.com
      INIT_SEAFILE_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${SEAFILE_ADMIN_PASSWORD}

      # on every start, so they stay SINGLE-valued at the canonical
      # name even though the Caddy site answers on the aliases too.

      # honest state of an install that does not include it.

      # seahub, the file server and WebDAV on one port.

    # reach it by address, so the links follow the address.
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        cat > /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf <<'CONF'
        server {
            listen 80;
            client_max_body_size 0;
            proxy_request_buffering off;
            location / {
                proxy_pass http://seafile:80;
                proxy_http_version 1.1;
                proxy_set_header Host $$http_host;
                proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
                proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto http;
                proxy_set_header Accept-Encoding "";
                proxy_redirect https://seafile.example.com/ /;
                proxy_read_timeout 1200s;
                sub_filter_types application/json text/javascript application/javascript;

        }

    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8188:80"

restart	restart	sudo docker compose -p photoprism restart
start	restart	sudo docker compose -p photoprism start
